notes: An unlearned caller sees C's exact "Yeah, right." after the declaration-list number(1,101) draw (R1/R2/R3).
A bare strike with no opponent is "Strike who?"; a named target that resolves to nobody is "They don't seem to be here."; both consume the shared percent draw.
The self target emits "You beat yourself about the face and neck." to the actor and the $n slaps $mself act to the room, then returns before damage() and WAIT_STATE.
The mount refusal precedes the roll and WAIT_STATE, so a resolvable target still sees only "Dismount first!".
The forced skill-1 arm proves set-155 miss_msg, zero-damage combat enrollment, and the unconditional three-pulse wait.
Damage flows through damage() at the C boundary; percent 100/101 still refuses by design, which is why the miss arm is carried by the deterministic skill-1 vehicle.
A 1-HP trainee drives POS_DEAD before skill_message: set-155 die_msg, XP before the death cry, and no invented corpse announcement.
C evaluates number(1,101) in do_strike's declaration list before one_argument and the GET_SKILL gate, so every invocation consumes one shared draw; the port drew nothing on that path.
Successful damage is the C integer conversion of GET_LEVEL(ch)*.65 with improve_skill deferred past the message dice.
A victim at or below POS_SLEEPING raises prob to 100, flipping a percent the awake skill value would refuse.
Both arms carry set 155 through the damage() boundary and emit no invented literal combat string.
At C_CMP skill_message writes CCYEL/CCNRM around the attacker line and CCRED/CCNRM around the victim line; default oracle normalization strips ANSI, so this is unit-covered.
C's AFF_CHARM/master arm needs a charmed player with a master; charm in this tree is mob-only and the port has no player master link, so the branch is unreachable from the command surface.
